messages:
devon: quick sync — console rollout tomorrow for header-based routing priority
anna: which header change exactly? the Workspace hint we discussed or the host header precedence?
devon: workspace_hint -> we added X-Workspace-Id as a hint header. change is: prefer explicit dedicated_pool assignment > X-Workspace-Id > VPC binding > host header. need to finalize ordering and fallback semantics.
samir: +1 to explicit pool winning. question: if pool assignment fails (quota or capacity), do we fallback to the workspace's dedicated_fallback_pool or to hosted? we need to be explicit so telemetry can tag the event.
jenna: proposal from my side: fallback order: 1) workspace's dedicated_fallback_pool (if configured and capacity), 2) regional hosted pool (with cost center set to workspace), 3) reject with 429 if workspace is under quota lock. that lets us surface cost and billback.
mike: agree on the list. also want a temporary canary toggle in console so we can flip behavior per workspace. UX: a per-workspace toggle 'Enforce Dedicated Routing' with an audit log entry when changed.
infra-bot: deploy-preview: routing-service:v2.3.4 — includes header-priority changes and telemetry hooks (trace-id preserved). See /deploy/1758009999
devon: telemetry needs two new tags on routed requests: routing_path (explicit_pool | workspace_pool | vpc_bound | host_fallback) and fallback_reason (quota | capacity | not_configured). surface counts in console dashboard.
samir: can we also add a histogram for time-to-route resolution? right now routing decision adds variable latency when checking pool capacity — we should alert if >50ms p95.
jenna: added a draft rule example for the gateway config (suggested format):
```
match: { headers: { X-Workspace-Id: present } }
route: { prefer: [explicit_pool, workspace_pool, host_header], fallback_policy: { capacity_check: true, fallback_order: [workspace_fallback, hosted_pool, reject] } }
```
mike: one more thing: when falling back to hosted, we need an opt-in privacy banner for customers with VPC/private endpoints so legal is OK with crossing to hosted. Add a console checkbox and a telemetry flag so we can report if hosted fallback happened.
devon: decision points for tomorrow:
- confirm precedence order (explicit_pool > workspace_hint > vpc_binding > host header) — seems settled
- confirm fallback order and 429 behavior — agreed on jenna's draft
- add console canary toggle + audit trail — mike to own
- add telemetry tags + latency histogram — samir to own
- add hosted-fallback privacy checkbox + legal annotation — jenna to coordinate

anna: i'll update the PR description with these bullets and link to the console mockups.
samir: i'll add a short eval in staging to induce capacity fail and capture routing_path counts.
jenna: will open a short RFC for the privacy wording.
mike: thanks — i'll sketch the console toggle in Figma and add the admin guardrails.
devon: great — meeting at 10. infra-bot will post the deploy link after staging runs. :thumbsup:
